{{Short description|Mathematical theorem}}
[[File:Gaussian distribution darts demonstration.svg|thumb|The gaussian correlation inequality states that probability of hitting both circle and rectangle with a dart is greater than or equal to the product of the individual probabilities of hitting the circle or the rectangle.]]
The '''Gaussian correlation inequality''' ('''GCI'''), formerly known as the '''Gaussian correlation conjecture''' ('''GCC'''),  is a [[mathematical theorem]] in the fields of [[mathematical statistics]] and [[convex geometry]]. 
==The statement==
The Gaussian correlation inequality states:

Let <math>\mu </math> be an ''n''-dimensional Gaussian probability measure on <math> \mathbb{R}^n </math>, i.e. <math>\mu</math> a [[multivariate normal distribution]], centered at the origin. Then for all [[convex set]]s <math> E,F \subset \mathbb{R}^n </math> that are [[symmetric set|symmetric about the origin]],

: <math> \mu(E \cap F) \geq \mu(E) \cdot \mu(F).</math>

As a simple example for ''n''=2, one can think of darts being thrown at a board, with their landing spots in the plane distributed according to a 2-variable normal distribution centered at the origin. (This is a reasonable assumption for any given darts player, with different players being described by different normal distributions.) If we now consider a circle and a rectangle in the plane, both centered at the origin, then the proportion of the darts landing in the intersection of both shapes is no less than the product of the proportions of the darts landing in each shape. This can also be formulated in terms of [[Conditional probability|conditional probabilities]]: if you're informed that your last dart hit the rectangle, then this information will increase your estimate of the probability that the dart hit the circle.

== History ==
A special case of the inequality was conjectured in 1955;<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Dunnett |first1=C. W. |last2=Sobel |first2=M. |date=1955 |title=Approximations to the probability integral and certain percentage points of a multivariate analogue of Student's t -distribution |journal=Biometrika |language=en |volume=42 |issue=1–2 |pages=258–267 |doi=10.1093/biomet/42.1-2.258 |issn=0006-3444}}</ref> further development was given by [[Olive Jean Dunn]] in 1958.<ref name="wolchover">{{cite web |last=Wolchover |first=Natalie |date=March 28, 2017 |title=A Long-Sought Proof, Found and Almost Lost |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/statistician-proves-gaussian-correlation-inequality-20170328/ |access-date=April 4, 2017 |publisher=QUANTA magazine}}</ref><ref name="annals1998">{{Cite journal |last1=Schechtman |first1=G. |last2=Schlumprecht |first2=Th. |last3=Zinn | first3=J.  |date=January 1998 |title=On the Gaussian measure of the intersection |journal=The Annals of Probability |volume=26 |issue=1 |pages=346–357 |doi=10.1214/aop/1022855422 |issn=0091-1798 |s2cid=119824731|doi-access=free }}</ref> The general case was stated in 1972, also as a conjecture.<ref>{{Cite conference |last1=Das Gupta |first1=S. |last2=Eaton |first2=M. L. |last3=Olkin |first3=I. |last4=Perlman |first4=M. |last5=Savage |first5=L. J. |last6=Sobel |first6=M. |date=1972 |title=Inequalities on the probability content of convex regions for elliptically contoured distributions |conference=Proceedings of the Sixth Berkeley Symposium on Mathematical Statistics and Probability |location=Berkeley, California |publisher=Univ. California Press |volume=II: Probability theory |pages=241–265}}</ref> The case of dimension ''n''=2 was proved in 1977<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Pitt |first=Loren D. |date=1977 |title=A Gaussian Correlation Inequality for Symmetric Convex Sets |journal=The Annals of Probability |volume=5 |issue=3 |pages=470–474 |doi= 10.1214/aop/1176995808|issn=|doi-access=free }}</ref> and certain special cases of higher dimension have also been proven in subsequent years.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Harge |first=Gilles |date=1999 |title=A Particular Case of Correlation Inequality for the Gaussian Measure |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/annals-of-probability/volume-27/issue-4/A-Particular-Case-of-Correlation-Inequality-for-the-Gaussian-Measure/10.1214/aop/1022874822.pdf |journal=The Annals of Probability |volume=27 |issue=4 |pages=1939–1951 |doi=10.1214/aop/1022874822 |s2cid=118789169 |issn=}}</ref>

The general case of the inequality remained open until 2014, when [[Thomas Royen]], a retired German statistician, proved it using relatively elementary tools.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Royen |first=Thomas |date=November 2014 |title=A simple proof of the Gaussian correlation conjecture extended to multivariate gamma distributions |url=http://www.pphmj.com/abstract/8713.htm |journal=Far East Journal of Theoretical Statistics |volume=48 |issue=2 |pages=139–145 |arxiv=1408.1028}}</ref> In fact, Royen generalized the conjecture and proved it for multivariate [[gamma distribution|gamma distributions]]. The proof did not gain attention when it was published in 2014, due to Royen's relative anonymity and the fact that the proof was published in the ''Far East Journal of Theoretical Statistics'', which was not a reputable journal in the field.<ref name="wolchover" /> Another reason was a history of false proofs (by others) and many failed attempts to prove the conjecture, causing skepticism among mathematicians in the field.<ref name="wolchover" />

The conjecture, and its solution, came to public attention in 2017, when other mathematicians described Royen's proof in a mainstream publication<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Latała |first1=R. |last2=Matlak |first2=D. |year=2017 |chapter=Royen's Proof of the Gaussian Correlation Inequality |title=Geometric Aspects of Functional Analysis |series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics |volume=2169 |pages=265–275 |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-45282-1_17 |arxiv=1512.08776|isbn=978-3-319-45281-4 |s2cid=36992343 }}</ref> and popular media reported on the story.<ref name="wolchover" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Farand |first=Chloe |date=2017-04-03 |title=Retired man solves one of hardest maths problems in the world and no one notices |language=en-GB |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/science/german-man-thomas-royen-solve-maths-problem-gaussian-correlation-inequality-retired-67-age-a7663936.html |access-date=2017-04-04}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dambeck |first=Holger |date=2017-04-04 |title=Erfolg mit 67 Jahren: Der Wunderopa der Mathematik |url=http://www.spiegel.de/wissenschaft/mensch/mathematiker-thomas-royen-beweist-mit-67-jahren-statistikproblem-gci-a-1141709.html |access-date=2017-04-04 |website=SPIEGEL ONLINE}}</ref>
